title: Avoiding Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Waste Lines
description: A frequent error in residential drainage installation is using a standard sanitary tee to join horizontal waste lines. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for horizontal-to-vertical transitions. When installed horizontally, the short-turn sweep fails to direct waste flow smoothly down the line, increasing the risk of clogs, solids accumulation, and splash-back into connecting lines. For horizontal-to-horizontal waste pipe connections, professional plumbing standards require a combination wye and 1/8 bend or a long-sweep wye fitting to maintain smooth fluid velocity and prevent blockages inside the pipe network.

Avoiding Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Waste Lines

A frequent error in residential drainage installation is using a standard sanitary tee to join horizontal waste lines. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for horizontal-to-vertical transitions. When installed horizontally, the short-turn sweep fails to direct waste flow smoothly down the line, increasing the risk of clogs, solids accumulation, and splash-back into connecting lines. For horizontal-to-horizontal waste pipe connections, professional plumbing standards require a combination wye and 1/8 bend or a long-sweep wye fitting to maintain smooth fluid velocity and prevent blockages inside the pipe network.
